Trick Room Support.description:
Set Details

  • Cresselia is the premier non-Restricted Trick Room setter of the format and boasts an amazing defensive profile thanks to its high stats and good ability, allowing it to sit in front of foes like Dialga and Groudon with ease while providing great support for its partners in the form of Trick Room, Helping Hand, and other options.

  • Trick Room and Psychic should be run on every Cresselia set; Trick Room provides immense support for Restricted Pokemon such as Kyogre and Dialga, while Psychic ensures that Cresselia isn't entirely vulnerable to Taunt. Helping Hand is always solid for boosting the power of Cresselia's Restricted partners, though Swagger is commonly run to bolster the power of allies such as Groudon and Rhyperior while also disrupting opposing Cresselia and other special attackers with confusion. The last move is commonly Light Screen to help Cresselia and its partners better handle Kyogre and Palkia, though Rest can be used as a solid healing option in conjunction with Chesto Berry, making Cresselia far harder to remove. This moveslot can be adjusted; Grass Knot, for example, can be used to deal solid chunks of damage to Groudon and Kyogre.

  • Sitrus Berry provides Cresselia with amazing burst healing, allowing it to stay on the field longer. This allows it to always turn Water Spout from Timid Splash Plate Kyogre into a 3HKO. Chesto Berry, on the other hand, allows Cresselia to avoid sleep from Smeargle, which would otherwise prevent it from setting Trick Room and could lead to disaster. Chesto Berry also works phenomenally with Rest, allowing Cresselia to heal a substantial amount without sacrificing two turns to sleep.

  • 0 Attack and Speed IVs allow Cresselia to take minimum damage from confusion and be as slow as possible, outspeeding other Cresselia in Trick Room. With maximum Special Defense, Cresselia becomes an insane wall, tanking hits from the strongest Pokemon in the format, including Kyogre, Palkia, and Dialga.

Teambuilding

  • Cresselia is able to tank attacks from many of the common Restricted Pokemon of the format, namely Groudon, Dialga, and Palkia. It can set Trick Room or Light Screen in front of them without fear, possibly even reversing Trick Room set by foes. It also does fabulously against non-Restricted Pokemon, such as Latios and Fighting-types like Infernape, Hariyama, and Toxicroak, though it must be cautious of Taunt.

  • Although Groudon usually struggles with Cresselia, a Helping Hand-boosted Fling can OHKO Cresselia if Groudon is holding the Iron Ball. Additionally, strong attackers like Kyogre in rain can overwhelm Cresselia, considering it usually cannot do much back. Tyranitar easily disposes of Cresselia with Crunch, being immune to Psychic and not taking much from even Grass Knot. Giratina similarly does lots of damage, while Leech Seed from Ludicolo or Abomasnow can exploit Cresselia's passive nature. Metagross is another threat, using Explosion to OHKO Cresselia and thus deny Trick Room or taking advantage of Trick Room itself thanks to Hammer Arm lowering its own Speed.

  • Kyogre and Ludicolo are partners that dispose of opposing Groudon, Kyogre, and Tyranitar with ease. Ludicolo can even switch into opposing Leech Seed. Dialga is another strong partner, doing nicely against Kyogre, Giratina, Ludicolo, and Abomasnow, as it resists their attacks and removes them with Choice Specs-boosted Draco Meteor or Dragon Pulse. Groudon has strong synergy with Cresselia, using Earthquake next to it freely thanks to Cresselia's Levitate. All of the mentioned partners greatly appreciate Cresselia's support from Trick Room and Helping Hand.

Rain Dance Sweeper.description:
Set Details

  • Ludicolo is one of the best partners to Kyogre. Permanent rain + Swift Swim enables Ludicolo to threaten massive damage before the opposing team can move. Its typing also allows Ludicolo to resist opposing Groudon's and Kyogre's STAB moves and super effectively deal damage to both. Ludicolo's middling Speed can be taken advantage of, as it can work inside Trick Room as well given the rain is not set up. Fake Out is instrumental in helping teammates set up or keep up the offensive pressure.

  • Ludicolo struggles to deal significant damage to Dragon-types such as Dialga, Palkia, and Latios. Blizzard can alleviate this problem a bit, as it provides unresisted damaged against said foes. Strong spread damage is usually uncommon but nonetheless helpful for Ludicolo, and Blizzard also helps in retaliating against Abomasnow leads.

  • Life Orb maximizes damage, being able to reliably OHKO Groudon and some Kyogre with Grass Knot. In particular, offensive Ludicolo can outrun Timid Choice Scarf Kyogre in the rain and almost always OHKO with Life Orb-boosted Grass Knot.

  • Maximum Speed investment makes Ludicolo faster than Choice Scarf base 90s such as Kyogre and Giratina as long as Swift Swim is active. Maximum Speed is also important in the mirror matchup, especially if both Ludicolos carry Fake Out.

  • Ludicolo can forgo the Swift Swim ability for Rain Dish, which enables it to operate on Trick Room teams very effectively as well as to recover from Life Orb damage.

  • Leech Seed and Protect have great natural synergy, preventing all damage as Ludicolo saps the life out of its foe. This can also soften foes to be finished off by a strong attack such as Hydro Pump. Even if Ludicolo faints or switches out, Leech Seed will still persist and help out the team by increasing their effective bulk.

Teambuilding

  • Most, if not all, teams with Ludicolo should have Kyogre as one of their Restricted Pokemon. Their natural synergy of Drizzle + Swift Swim off the bat is very reliable as a lead. One of Kyogre's natural checks is Groudon in sun, and Ludicolo is able to threaten a 2HKO with Grass Knot.

  • Trick Room setters such as Dialga and Cresselia can also be very effective when Ludicolo is outside of rain due to Ludicolo's below-average Speed stat. Dialga is an especially good partner for Ludicolo, as it is a great check against opposing Dragon-type Pokemon that Ludicolo commonly struggles against.

  • Ludicolo loves getting off a parting Leech Seed before switching out or getting KOed. Pokemon that stay on the field for a long time such as Cresselia and Giratina are prime targets for Leech Seed. Bulky teammates such as Dialga and Metagross appreciate switching into Pokemon hit by Leech Seed for the extra recovery.

  • As mentioned, Dragon-types, especially Palkia and Dialga, most commonly give Ludicolo trouble, as they can threaten massive damage with Draco Meteor while not being scared much in retaliation.

  • Abomasnow is one of the most consistent answers against Dragon-type Pokemon, especially when under Trick Room. Snow Warning enables perfectly accurate Blizzards for Ludicolo as well. However, opposing Abomasnow can give Ludicolo trouble. They resist Ludicolo's STAB moves, replace rain with hail, and wear down Ludicolo with Blizzards.

  • Togekiss can use Follow Me, which shields Ludicolo's would-be targets such as opposing Kyogre and Groudon. Without Blizzard or Hydro Pump, Ludicolo cannot threaten much damage, while Air Slash from Togekiss is a 2HKO.

  • When leading offensive Ludicolo + Kyogre, Trick Room Dialga and Iron Ball Groudon + Jumpluff are the most difficult leads to deal with, as your damage is significantly mitigated while your opponent is threatening speed control.

Bulky Support.description:
Set Details

  • Bulky support Ludicolo utilizes Ludicolo's great defensive movepool to soften foes for other sweepers such as offensive Trick Room Dialga and Ho-Oh. Despite minimal offensive investment, Ludicolo still has has positive matchups into Kyogre, Groudon, and Tyranitar thanks to STAB Grass Knot.

  • Leech Seed is Ludicolo's primary tool at threatening opposing Pokemon. Taking consistent damage at the end of every turn can be an extreme nuisance and force the opponent's Pokemon to switch out. This bulky Ludicolo is much better equipped to make use of the extra healing provided by Leech Seed in conjunction with Protect to stay on the field for longer. Ludicolo's partners still enjoy the added chip damage and healing all the same.

  • Fake Out is great to let Ludicolo's partners set up; usually they set up Trick Room.

  • Icy Wind is also a worthwhile option on Ludicolo to provide a form of speed control to the rest of the team. Mid-Speed Restricted Pokemon such as Ho-Oh especially appreciate the support.

  • Sitrus Berry leverages Ludicolo's good resistances and Leech Seed in order to stick on the field for longer. Even if Ludicolo takes a lot of damage from a single attack such as Palkia's Spacial Rend, Sitrus Berry + Leech Seed can restore a lot of lost HP.

  • 220 Speed EVs still let Ludicolo outspeed Timid Choice Scarf Kyogre and similar Choice Scarf base 90s with Swift Swim. Ludicolo is able to use Fake Out before opposing Weavile and Infernape while under the rain as well.

  • With a Calm nature and HP investment, Ludicolo can survive powerful attacks from Kyogre, Dialga, and Palkia. The Special Attack investment is mandatory to always 2HKO specially defensive Groudon.

Teambuilding

  • While Kyogre is still extremely recommended on teams with Ludicolo, support Ludicolo does not need the rain as desperately, as it does not rely on Hydro Pump for damage or Swift Swim as much for speed control.

  • Redirection and fast Fake Out Pokemon such as Togekiss, Infernape, and Weavile can effectively prevent Ludicolo from disrupting foes with Leech Seed and Fake Out. Grass Knot as its only significant form of direct damage makes Ludicolo unable to break through most of these Pokemon.

  • Ludicolo is also very vulnerable to Explosion and Self-Destruct. A Ludicolo without Hydro Pump is a sitting duck against a well-timed Self-Destruct from Snorlax or Explosion from Metagross or Azelf.

  • Ho-Oh becomes a massive threat when Ludicolo successfully removes opposing Kyogre, Tyranitar, and Groudon. While Ho-Oh's Speed is middling, it makes it flexible for many forms of speed control, including Icy Wind. Ho-Oh also can add on extra chip damage and extend survivability thanks to Sacred Fire burns in addition to Leech Seed.

  • Dialga can be extremely potent when paired with Ludicolo. Fake Out can enable it to set up Trick Room, and Leech Seed will prolong Dialga's already great longevity. Dialga also has a rare resistance to Explosion, making it very well-suited to deal with such teams.

Standard Offensive.description:
Set Details

  • Kyogre is the most defining Pokemon in the format. It boasts extremely high Special Attack, very respectable bulk, and Drizzle to power up its already monstrous Water-type STAB attacks. Kyogre is as unpredictable as it is powerful; it can vary its moves and item choice to suit nearly any team's needs.

  • Water Spout is Kyogre's strongest move; at full health, a rain-boosted, single-target, Choice Specs-boosted Water Spout is capable of OHKOing Calm Cresselia. Thunder hits Water-type foes such as Kyogre, Palkia, and Ludicolo. Thunder's chance to inflict paralysis is a very powerful bonus that can further cripple the aforementioned threats.

  • Blizzard hits common foes such as Abomasnow, Giratina, and Groudon. It is often used with Abomasnow on the team, but can even take advantage of enemy Abomasnow's hail to be perfectly accurate. Ice Beam is an alternative, more consistent move but lacks the explosive spread damage power of Blizzard.

  • Muddy Water is used on Choice item Kyogre as an alternative Water-type attack at low health. Surf is a more accurate option that can be used alongside Dry Skin users like Toxicroak or Water-resistant Pokemon like Ludicolo, Palkia, or Abomasnow. Life Orb Kyogre should run Protect instead, but that does not preclude Kyogre from having a Choice item swapped onto it.

  • Choice Scarf transforms Kyogre into an oppressive sweeper capable of outspeeding most unboosted threats and dealing tremendous damage with Water Spout, allowing it to act before foes and thus use Water Spout at full power. With Choice Specs or Life Orb, Kyogre relies more on team support to control the speed order in the battle, but in return, it can break through even the bulkiest enemies such as Tyranitar, Dialga, and Cresselia.

  • Modest nature maximizes the damage output that Kyogre offers, while maximum Speed is required to outpace Smeargle. Timid nature improves Kyogre's matchup against common threats like opposing Kyogre, Groudon, Dialga, and Giratina. Timid nature is mostly used on Life Orb or Choice Specs sets.

Teambuilding

  • The Dragon-type restricted Pokemon Dialga, Palkia, and Giratina, along with Ludicolo, are the best checks to Kyogre. With their excellent bulk and resistance to Water, they shrug off Kyogre's Water-type attacks and can return fire with strong moves. Ludicolo stands out, as it can outspeed even Choice Scarf Kyogre with its Swift Swim ability and KO it with Life Orb-boosted Grass Knot. Toxicroak is immune to Water-type attacks thanks to its Dry Skin ability, but it has to fear Thunder.

  • Opposing weather from Groudon or Tyranitar can weaken Kyogre, enable their teammates to endure Kyogre's attacks, and potentially disrupt Kyogre's teammates that rely on rain. Abomasnow, in addition to overwriting Kyogre's weather, can resist Water Spout and in return deal substantial damage with Grass Knot.

  • Kyogre relies on moving first to deal maximum damage with Water Spout. Accordingly, faster threats like Infernape, Weavile, opposing Choice Scarf Kyogre, or Palkia can pose significant challenges to Kyogre, as can Trick Room teams.

  • Ludicolo benefits tremendously from Kyogre's Drizzle ability and, in turn, can support Kyogre with Fake Out while also being a powerful sweeper unto itself with Grass Knot or rain-boosted Hydro Pump.

  • Fake Out support from Toxicroak or Hitmontop gives Kyogre crucial turns with which to deal damage, and their Fighting-type attacks can help Kyogre against common threats such as Dialga, Tyranitar, and Abomasnow.

  • Togekiss offers Follow Me for redirection, speed control with Thunder Wave, and Helping Hand support while also having a very good matchup against Ludicolo. Life Orb Kyogre particularly benefits from the speed control of Thunder Wave, while Choice Specs Kyogre can make use of Helping Hand to deal even greater damage. Choice Scarf Kyogre can appreciate Encore to punish Trick Room and Extreme Speed to break the Focus Sash of threats like Smeargle, Infernape, and Weavile.

  • Giratina is a unique partner to Kyogre, offering Tailwind support on more offensive Explosion-based strategies. Giratina can also check enemy Ludicolo and Cresselia very effectively.

Trick Room Sweeper.description:
Set Details

  • Kyogre is a premier attacker on Trick Room teams, as its extremely powerful Water Spout makes the most of Trick Room's limited turns. Furthermore, as Kyogre does not need to invest in Speed, it can instead bolster its already excellent bulk and become even more difficult to remove. Kyogre can eliminate key threats to Trick Room such as Metagross and Tyranitar due to its positive type matchup.

  • In Trick Room, Kyogre will almost always act first and can use a full-power Water Spout if it is at full health. Thunder and Blizzard are the best coverage options for dealing with enemies that Water Spout cannot hit effectively.

  • Macho Brace ensures Kyogre is as slow as possible so it can act first during Trick Room. Kyogre runs minimum Speed IVs and can even be used at level 49 to ensure that it acts first in Trick Room against enemy Kyogre with Macho Brace or Groudon with Iron Ball. Macho Brace is preferred over Iron Ball to allow Trick Room support Pokemon such as Bronzong or Cresselia to use Skill Swap on Kyogre, resetting the weather and granting Kyogre the Levitate ability.

Teambuilding

  • Slower threats, such as Rhyperior, Parasect, Iron Ball Abomasnow, or Iron Ball Tyranitar, can pose significant issues for Kyogre, but if Kyogre can stall out the turns of its own Trick Room, then it will have the advantage in regular battle conditions.

  • Thanks to their typings, Ludicolo and Palkia are very strong defensively against Kyogre and can deal substantial damage to it; however, due to their high Speed, they can suffer during Trick Room.

  • As Kyogre is reliant on Trick Room to function, it will be far less effective if Trick Room is prevented by Taunt. Supportive Pokemon such as Togekiss or Smeargle are often crucial for helping teammates consistently set up Trick Room.

  • Kyogre cannot set Trick Room for itself, so it needs support from Cresselia or Dialga to function. Cresselia has incredible bulk that makes it the most consistent Trick Room setter in the format. Dialga, on the other hand, can offer both Trick Room support and offensive synergy with Kyogre, as it can deal with threats like Ludicolo, Abomasnow, and Palkia, whereas Kyogre can deal with Groudon, Tyranitar, and Metagross. Bronzong is an alternative Trick Room setter, but it is less popular than Cresselia due to its lower bulk and lack of access to Helping Hand.

  • Other Trick Room attackers like Metagross, Abomasnow, and Rhyperior can make the most of the Trick Room turns alongside Kyogre. Abomasnow, in particular, is a strong partner, as it can set hail, which both overwrites opposing sun that can neuter Kyogre's Water Spout and makes Blizzard perfectly accurate.

Set Details

  • Groudon is one of the strongest Trick Room sweepers in the VGC 2010 metagame, capable of threatening huge damage onto common Pokemon like Dialga and Tyranitar while overriding the respective weathers of the likes of Kyogre and Abomasnow. Being a physically biased Restricted Pokemon, it is able to target the lower Defense stats of foes like Kyogre while tanking hits from other physical attackers like Metagross.

  • Rock Slide enables Groudon to hit Ho-Oh and Abomasnow for good damage. Fling is commonly run with Iron Ball to make it a high-power option. Not only does it get rid of Iron Ball in a pinch, but it also deals significant damage to Cresselia and Giratina-O, both of which are immune to Earthquake and can shrug off Rock Slide. Fling OHKOes opposing Cresselia, Giratina, and Ludicolo when Groudon receives a Helping Hand boost from a partner such as Cresselia. Swords Dance is more commonly run when using Lum Berry, allowing Groudon to have good odds at OHKOing uninvested Kyogre with Earthquake.

  • Fire Punch can be used to OHKO Abomasnow that forgo Occa Berry and deal damage to Ludicolo and Bronzong. This comes at the cost of Fling, which means Groudon is forced to trade huge burst damage for more consistent damage over time. Substitute is another option over Fling or Swords Dance used to punish defensive play by making Groudon harder to remove, though it prevents Groudon from hitting Giratina hard and limits its offensive capabilities.

  • Iron Ball cuts Groudon's Speed, which makes it a strong Trick Room option by notably letting it outspeed Abomasnow and Tyranitar under Trick Room. Lum Berry, on the other hand, allows Groudon to avoid burns and sleep from Ho-Oh and Smeargle, respectively. Lum Berry also enables Groudon to be inflicted by an ally's Swagger, which turns it into a devastating sweeper.

  • The given EV Spread maximizes Groudon's Attack and bulk, letting it survive Water Spout from Life Orb Modest Kyogre in the sun and avoid a 2HKO from Timid Latios's Psychic. 0 Speed IVs and a Brave nature are used to make Groudon as slow as possible for Trick Room, though 31 Speed IVs and an Adamant nature can be used to outspeed opposing Groudon outside of it.

Teambuilding

  • Kyogre and Palkia threaten Groudon with Water Spout and Hydro Pump, respectively, and both of them are to OHKO Groudon when the sun isn't up. Choice Specs Kyogre even OHKOes Groudon through the sun with Ice Beam and has good odds to do so with Blizzard, while Choice Specs Palkia can do so with Draco Meteor or Blizzard. Other strong special attackers like Dialga and Latios threaten to OHKO Groudon with Choice Specs-boosted Draco Meteor before it can move.

  • Grass-type Pokemon, namely Abomasnow and Ludicolo, pose a huge threat to Groudon, with both examples being able to use Grass Knot to threaten an OHKO. The former of the two can override the sun with hail, leaving Groudon more vulnerable to Water-type attacks from the likes of Palkia. Groudon can OHKO Ludicolo with a Helping Hand-boosted Fling, but it must be wary of Protect.

  • Cresselia or another Restricted Pokemon that can set Trick Room, namely Dialga, is a must-have for Groudon. Trick Room solves Groudon's Speed issue and allows it to threaten faster foes like opposing Dialga with Earthquake before they can move. Cresselia can provide support in Helping Hand to boost the damage output of Groudon, sit next to Groudon while it uses Earthquake, and use Swagger on Lum Berry variants to boost their Attack, while Dialga is able to help out against Palkia, Kyogre, and Grass-types thanks to its typing and power.

  • Answers to Kyogre such as Abomasnow and Ludicolo help out a lot, as they threaten big damage onto Kyogre with Grass Knot. The former can hit Latios and other Dragon-types like Rayquaza with Blizzard and use Leech Seed to bring bulkier foes like Cresselia and Giratina into KO range of Fling, while the latter can use Fake Out to help Groudon set up with Swords Dance or help Cresselia safely set up Trick Room. Outside of Trick Room, Jumpluff can take advantage of the sun to become the fastest Pokemon on the field thanks to Chlorophyll; it can put foes to sleep with Sleep Powder, which allows Groudon to safely attack or set up.

Trick Room Attacker.description:
Set Details

  • Dialga leverages its great bulk and strong defensive typing to safely set up Trick Room in the face of metagame staples such as Kyogre, Giratina, and Palkia, greatly benefiting itself as well as supporting its team while having a strong offensive presence with its Dragon-type STAB moves and an excellent Special Attack.

  • Earth Power allows for Dialga to threaten the Steel-types that resist Dragon Pulse, most notably Metagross, while also hitting opposing Dialga and Tyranitar for sizeable damage. Thunder lets Dialga hit Kyogre super effectively. Fire Blast can be used as a powerful coverage option for Metagross and Abomasnow, whereas Blizzard is a strong spread attack under Abomasnow's hail, importantly threatening Groudon.

  • Chople Berry allows for Dialga to survive Infernape's or Hitmontop's Close Combat, which would otherwise threaten an OHKO. Lum Berry lets Dialga take a Spore from Parasect, Dark Void from Smeargle, or Sleep Powder from Jumpluff. Leftovers gives Dialga more longevity, allowing it to be more effective late-game.

  • 252 Special Attack EVs maximize Dialga's offensive presence, while the rest goes into bulk. 0 Speed IVs help Dialga outspeed other 90 base Speed foes under Trick Room, such as Groudon, Kyogre, and opposing Dialga. 252 HP and 228 Special Defense EVs allow for Dialga to survive Draco Meteor from opposing Choice Specs Dialga, two Water Spouts from Life Orb Kyogre, or two Blizzards from Life Orb Abomasnow.

Teambuilding

  • Dialga matches up strongly against Kyogre and its common partners such as Ludicolo, resisting their attacks and doing large damage back with Dragon Pulse and Thunder. It also matches up well against Cresselia and Abomasnow, neither of which can threaten Dialga back with meaningful damage.

  • Groudon is particularly threatening towards Dialga, being able to take its Dragon-type STAB moves and threaten back with huge super effective damage off Earthquake. Infernape, Toxicroak, Hariyama, and Hitmontop can also be difficult for Dialga, as they all can threaten non-Chople Berry sets for huge damage with their Fighting-type STAB moves, as well as use Fake Out, and Taunt in the case of Infernape, to prevent Trick Room. Metagross and Tyranitar additionally both threaten Dialga with Hammer Arm and Low Kick, respectively.

  • One of Dialga's best partners is Smeargle, as Fake Out and Follow Me help protect Dialga while it sets Trick Room, which Smeargle in turn can use to outspeed foes and incapacitate them with Dark Void. Togekiss also supports Dialga through Follow Me while threatening Fighting-types with Air Slash.

  • Dialga also pairs phenomenally with Kyogre, which can OHKO Groudon, Infernape, and Tyranitar with rain-boosted Water-type STAB moves, though you need to position carefully around Groudon's Drought; Kyogre enjoys Dialga's Trick Room support, especially with Iron Ball sets, as well as its ability to handle the Dragon-types that can take Kyogre's attacks such as Palkia and Giratina. Additionally, Snorlax and Abomasnow both greatly appreciate Dialga's Trick Room, and the latter can threaten Groudon with its Ice-type STAB moves.

Fast Offensive.description:
Set Details

  • Dialga, with its stellar Special Attack, wide movepool, and excellent defensive typing, is a commanding offensive threat. Thanks to its unique typing, Dialga can withstand attacks from Kyogre, a dominant force in the format, while being an offensive force in and of itself. Dialga’s endless type coverage means its moveset can adapt to meet the needs of the team it is on.

  • Draco Meteor is Dialga’s most powerful move, providing burst damage that can OHKO even neutral targets with Choice Specs. Dragon Pulse is most often used on Choice Specs sets to provide a consistent and accurate option.

  • Earth Power is excellent coverage to hit enemy Dialga, Metagross, and Tyranitar for excellent damage. Fire Blast and Overheat can hit Abomasnow, Metagross, and Bronzong particularly hard, with Overheat also benefitting from White Herb to reset stat drops. These Fire-type moves can be further powered up by Groudon’s Drought.

  • Blizzard is a strong spread damage attack that can deal huge damage to both opponents, especially in hail. Thunder is particularly strong against Kyogre and Ludicolo, as with a Helping Hand boost, even defensively invested Kyogre will be KOed by Choice Specs-boosted Thunder. Protect is only used on sets without a Choice item.

  • Choice Specs empowers Dialga to OHKO all but the bulkiest enemies with Draco Meteor or to deal consistent damage with Dragon Pulse. White Herb lets Dialga use a full-power Draco Meteor or Overheat a second time while crucially allowing Dialga to switch moves so that it may use Protect and is less susceptible to being PP stalled by Pressure. White Herb can be triggered by enemies with the Intimidate ability; however, it is relatively uncommon in the format.

  • Alternative items such as Life Orb, Sitrus Berry, and Choice Scarf may be considered. Life Orb has the notable downside of cutting into Dialga’s excellent natural bulk. Choice Scarf Dialga can lack the decisive power to achieve KOs from full health, but it excels at finishing off weakened targets.

  • A Modest nature enables Dialga to OHKO offensive Trick Room Dialga and fast Kyogre with Draco Meteor as well as 3HKO Sitrus Berry Cresselia most of the time with Dragon Pulse. Maximum Speed investment ensures that Dialga outpaces Focus Sash Smeargle and can Speed tie with enemy Dialga, Kyogre, and Giratina. With a White Herb, Dialga can run more defensive investment, but it still should use a Modest nature.

Teambuilding

  • Palkia can be a significant threat to Dialga. With a Haban Berry, Palkia survives Choice Specs-boosted Dragon Pulse. With Choice Specs of its own, Palkia will outspeed and OHKO Dialga.

  • Metagross, Tyranitar, and Snorlax threaten Dialga with Hammer Arm, Low Kick, and Superpower, respectively, without fearing much damage in return. They may also take advantage of Trick Room to act first against Dialga.

  • Fighting-types like Infernape, Toxicroak, and Hariyama, as well as Ground-types like Groudon and Rhyperior, can deal even more damage against Dialga. They will, however, usually fail to OHKO Dialga with unboosted attacks due to Dialga's excellent natural bulk and will be OHKOed in return by a powered-up Draco Meteor.

  • Kyogre is an excellent partner for Dialga, as it can remove Metagross, Tyranitar, Infernape, and Rhyperior with ease. Kyogre benefits from Dialga checking enemy Giratina, Ludicolo, and Kyogre.

  • Togekiss and Smeargle support Dialga very effectively. Togekiss can redirect powerful attacks like Draco Meteor from enemy Dragon-types as well as Fake Out to ensure that Dialga gets to attack. Togekiss can further boost the power of Dialga by using Helping Hand, letting it OHKO even the bulkiest foes like Cresselia or Kyogre. Additionally, Togekiss is a very strong check to Fighting-types like Infernape and Toxicroak; it can even run a Choice Scarf set to safeguard against enemy Smeargle or Air Slash to disrupt the enemy. Smeargle, on the other hand, is a very dangerous disruptor with Fake Out, Dark Void, Follow Me, and endless other possible moves. Choice Scarf Smeargle stands out as an effective partner for Dialga on lead, as it can force the enemy to deal with it first while Dialga freely dishes out damage.

  • Cresselia can be an effective support for offensive Dialga. It can use Thunder Wave to cripple the enemy and has excellent type synergy with Dialga, being able to take on Fighting- and Ground-types with ease.
